title: Mending Lane · rustic world, colour restored

sampling.method: Equal contribution per image. Whole landscape paintings; upper 40% of portrait paintings to exclude their intentionally dark text area. RGB median-cut representatives; these are not literal source-pixel hex values.

rules: Tune contrast and saturation per sprite at map scale; readability matters as much as palette adherence. Preserve useful source shades, dark contours and lit surfaces instead of reducing colour count to force a match. The original chest and unchanged well are contrast references; retain the approved apple treatment and the helpful olive correction to bright green trees.

Ground textures should be light and desaturated so objects stand out. Suggest darker places through quieter colour rather than darkening the canvas; interactables need separated shadows, midtones and highlights without becoming muddy or washed out.

The main contrast is state and meaning: natural or pre-restoration assets stay in the muted post-apocalyptic rustic world palette; player-restored assets, the player and special/sacred places may deliberately depart from it. Style stays consistently chibi retro pixel in every state.
Use the current 16px Cyan character pack as the sprite style reference: compact rounded proportions, readable dark contours, sparse purposeful pixel clusters and opaque pixel edges.

Use story art for colour relationships and atmosphere, not its illustration detail density. The paintings are golden-hour scenes; ordinary game foliage needs an adapted muted green ramp, not an orange tint over everything.

For a common 16px plant, aim for 3–5 opaque colours including outline, with one dominant midtone and separated shadow/highlight. For a tree canopy, aim for 4–6 colours in large rounded clusters; bark gets its own small ramp. These are review targets, not hard limits.

Keep source-pixel density comparable to the character pack. Prefer authored 16px small props and 32×48 trees; size is a starting point, not a ban on larger art. Do not shrink painterly assets until their detail becomes noise.
Ordinary grass, shrubs and tree foliage use olive/moss relationships. Nearby shades are acceptable when hue, contrast and saturation still belong to the same ramp; exact hex matching is not required.
Use warm stone greys, dark cracks and a few light broken faces for ruins. Reserve amber for small lit edges; ruins should not compete with characters and rewards.

Player cyan is an intentional exception. Flowers may use muted rose, lilac or blue on petals, with ordinary green stems. Restored assets, sacred places, magical mushrooms and rare finds may depart further when colour communicates their state or special role.
Judge the silhouette first at native pixel size and then at runtime size on both light grass and dark ground. Palette changes cannot fix a fuzzy outline, unreadable silhouette or excessive texture.
Keep current shipped art until a replacement is selected. The palette is an art-review target, not a runtime quantization filter or an automatic recolouring instruction.

worldStates.name: Natural / unrestored
worldStates.rule: Muted rustic palette. Olive/moss foliage, warm earth, weathered stone and restrained highlights. Applies to common flora and pre-restoration ruins.
worldStates.exceptions: Flowers may use small coloured petals. A natural object only breaks further from the palette when it has a specific special or sacred role.

worldStates.name: Player / restored
worldStates.rule: Deliberate off-palette contrast: cleaner cool hues, brighter accents and clearer material surfaces communicate care and change. Preserve some warm-world colours for continuity.
worldStates.exceptions: This is permission, not a requirement to make every restored object saturated. Preserve the same pixel density, contours and silhouette language.

worldStates.name: Special / sacred
worldStates.rule: Distinct accent families can identify meaningful places or rare finds before interaction. One dominant accent family per place; not a rainbow across every prop.
worldStates.exceptions: A natural sacred grove can be an intentional exception; its special role should explain its departure from ordinary wild foliage.

ruinsPlan.use: Main masonry silhouette after contour cleanup; rubble pile can supply a quieter secondary shape.
A clearer pale finish can identify a special or restored site while the surrounding unrestored debris stays warm and muted.

spritePlan.status: Default recolours applied; zone-specific alternatives remain proposals
spritePlan.note: Original and Applied views share the exact source pixels. Six default palettes are applied in-game, including matching tree growth and broken-pot states. Zone alternatives remain preview-only; there are no seasonal rules.
